questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# verify:fast and verify:full (D4). Usage: verify.sh fast|full
set -u
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"

case "${1:-}" in
  fast) cmd=$(cfg VERIFY_FAST) || exit 1 ;;
  full) cmd=$(cfg VERIFY_FULL) || exit 1 ;;
  *) echo "ERROR: Unknown tier. Use: verify.sh fast|full" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
cd "$ROOT" || exit 1

# The PreToolUse hook does not see test changes that Bash makes. The baseline check finds them.
# A lock failure does not stop the checks, so the caller sees every result.
"$DIR/test-lock.sh" check
lock=$?
bash -c "$cmd" || exit
exit "$lock"
# Project values for the kit hooks. Copy to .claude/project.sh. The hooks source it. Do not run it.
# Give one line for each area, with a comment that names the area and its tool.

# Test files: extended regexes on repo-relative paths. The test lock blocks edits to each match.
# Include test setup and e2e files. If the agent can change them, a test can pass without a fix.
TEST_PATTERNS=(
  '^packages/[^/]+/tests/'   # all packages: pytest
)

# Formats one file after each edit. $1 is the repo-relative path. It runs at the repo root.
# Delete this function if the project has no formatter.
format() {
  case "$1" in
    *.py) uv run ruff format -q "$1" && uv run ruff check --fix -q "$1" ;;
  esac
}

Base directory for this skill: /Users/janeshorst/.claude-mutinex/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.4.1/skills/brainstorming

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by classifying how much process the request needs, then work
through your path: understand the context, refine the idea, present a
design, and get your human partner's approval.

## Establish Shared Understanding

The outcome of brainstorming is an understanding your human partner can
recognize and correct, grounded in what they want to accomplish.

1. **Discover intent.** Use the request and available context to identify
   the intended outcome, who it is for, and what success looks like. When
   that information is missing, ask one focused question about purpose or
   intended use before proposing features or an approach. Knowing the app
   genre does not tell you why your partner wants it. Gathering missing
   requirements does not ask them to authorize the task again.
2. **Write back your understanding.** Summarize the intended outcome,
   relevant constraints, and success criteria in a short note your partner
   can assess. Separate what they said from assumptions. Invite correction
   and incorporate their answer before treating this as the design brief.
3. **Carry intent into the design.** Preserve the agreed understanding in
   the selected path's design artifact: the written spec for architectural
   work, or the in-chat design/probe for bounded work and spikes. Check
   proposed features and technical choices against that understanding.

When the request already supplies the purpose and constraints, reflect
that understanding instead of asking the same questions again. Keep the
note concise; its accuracy and the opportunity to correct it matter.

<HARD-GATE>
Before taking any implementation action, including invoking an
implementation skill, writing product code, scaffolding, installing
product dependencies, or creating an external project, complete the
selected path's prerequisites:

- Spike: the human partner approves the question and probe.
- Bounded: the human partner approves the short in-chat design.
- Architectural: the human partner reviews and approves the written spec,
  then reviews the written implementation plan and selects its execution
  method. Conversational design approval only permits writing the spec;
  written-spec approval only permits invoking writing-plans.

A reply approves the stage actually presented. Approval of an idea or
feature scope does not approve artifacts that do not exist yet. Resume
at the earliest incomplete stage; do not turn one approval into permission
to skip the rest of the selected path. Read-only project exploration is
allowed while those prerequisites remain incomplete.
</HARD-GATE>

## Three Paths

Before your first question, classify the request and say the
classification out loud — "this looks bounded, so I'll present a short
design here rather than write a spec" — so your human partner can
override it:

- **Spike** — a feasibility question ("can we...", "is it possible...",
  "quick and dirty is fine") whose output is an answer, not code you
  keep. Present the question and what you'll try in 2-3 sentences, get
  a nod, then find out as cheaply as correctness allows. No design
  doc, no spec file. Report findings as a recommendation; anything you
  built stays labeled throwaway.
- **Bounded** — a well-scoped change to code that already exists in
  this repo: a new flag, a small endpoint, a one-file fix.
  Understanding the kind of app is not enough — bounded means the flow
  you are changing is already here to read. If there is no existing
  flow to change, the task is not bounded. Ask the clarifying
  questions that matter, present a short design IN CHAT (a few
  sentences to a few short paragraphs), and STOP. Implementation
  starts only after your human partner says yes to that design — a
  bounded task's approval is as hard a gate as an architectural
  one. No spec file, no implementation plan document.
- **Architectural** — new projects, new subsystems, changes that
  restructure how components fit together or alter interfaces others
  depend on. Follow the full process: questions, approaches, sectioned
  design, written spec, then the writing-plans skill.

When in doubt between two paths, take the heavier one. The ratchet is
one-way: hidden complexity discovered mid-task upgrades the path —
stop, say so, and step up. Nothing downgrades mid-task.

## Anti-Pattern: "Too Simple To Need Approval"

Every path ends with your human partner approving the required design
before implementation. A bounded change may need only two sentences in
chat. A new todo-list project is architectural and requires the written
spec and planning handoffs. Scale the artifact to the selected path;
complete that path's reviews before implementation.

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is too simple to need a design" | Follow the selected path: a bounded change gets a short chat design; an architectural change gets the written spec and planning handoffs. |
| "I'll call it bounded and skip the spec" | Reaching for a label to skip work IS the doubt — take the heavier path. |
| "It's bounded and the design is obvious — I'll start while they read it" | The gate is the approval, not the design's length. Present, then stop until you hear yes. |
| "I understand this kind of app, so it's bounded" | Bounded measures the repo, not your familiarity. A new project has no existing flow — it is architectural. |
| "The spike works, so I'll keep the code" | A spike's output is an answer. Keeping the code is a new request — classify it. |
| "It grew, but I'm almost done — no need to re-classify" | Hidden complexity upgrades the path mid-task. Stop and say so. |
| "They approved the spike, so the follow-up change is approved too" | Each task gets its own classification and its own approval. |

## Checklist

Classify first, announce the path, then create a task for each item on
your path and complete them in order.

**Spike:**
1. **Explore project context** — enough to frame the probe
2. **Present question + probe plan** — 2-3 sentences
3. **Get approval** — a nod is enough
4. **Investigate** — as cheaply as correctness allows
5. **Report findings** — a recommendation; label anything built as throwaway

**Bounded:**
1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, the ones that matter
3. **Present short design in chat** — approach, files touched, testing
4. **Get approval** — STOP and wait for an explicit yes; presenting the design and starting in the same breath is skipping the gate
5. **Implement** — proceed with the normal development workflow (TDD applies); no plan document

**Architectural:**
1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer the visual companion just-in-time** — NOT upfront. The first time a question would genuinely be clearer shown than described, offer it then (its own message); on approval its browser tab opens for you. If no visual question ever arises, never offer it. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec self-review** — quick inline check for placeholders, contradictions, ambiguity, scope (see below)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" [shape=diamond];
    "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" [shape=box];
    "Present short design in chat" [shape=box];
    "Human approves?" [shape=diamond];
    "Investigate; report recommendation" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Implement via normal workflow (no plan doc)" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" [shape=box];
    "User reviews spec?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Hidden complexity? Upgrade path" [shape=box];

    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" [label="spike"];
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" [label="bounded"];
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Explore project context" [label="architectural"];
    "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" -> "Human approves?";
    "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" -> "Present short design in chat";
    "Present short design in chat" -> "Human approves?";
    "Human approves?" -> "Investigate; report recommendation" [label="spike: yes"];
    "Human approves?" -> "Implement via normal workflow (no plan doc)" [label="bounded: yes"];
    "Hidden complexity? Upgrade path" -> "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural";
    "Explore project context" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)";
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" -> "User reviews spec?";
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Write design doc" [label="changes requested"];
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill" [label="approved"];
}
```

**Terminal states are path-bound.** Architectural: the ONLY skill you
invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans — never frontend-design,
mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. Bounded: after
approval, implementation proceeds directly through the normal
development workflow; no plan document. Spike: the terminal state is a
reported recommendation.

## The Process

The subsections below serve the bounded and architectural paths (a
spike stops at "present the probe, get a nod"). Sections from
**Exploring approaches** onward are architectural-path depth — for
bounded work, context plus a few questions plus a short in-chat design
is the whole process.

**Understanding the idea:**

- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.
- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**

- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why
- YAGNI ruthlessly - remove unnecessary features from every approach and design

**Presenting the design:**

- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Design for isolation and clarity:**

- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.

**Working in existing codebases:**

- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
- Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.

## After the Design (architectural path)

**Documentation:**

- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Spec Self-Review:**
After writing the spec document, look at it with fresh eyes:

1. **Placeholder scan:** Any "TBD", "TODO", incomplete sections, or vague requirements? Fix them.
2. **Internal consistency:** Do any sections contradict each other? Does the architecture match the feature descriptions?
3. **Scope check:** Is this focused enough for a single implementation plan, or does it need decomposition?
4. **Ambiguity check:** Could any requirement be interpreted two different ways? If so, pick one and make it explicit.

Fix any issues inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on.

**User Review Gate:**
After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:

> "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."

Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.

**Implementation:**

- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Visual Companion

A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.

**Offering the companion (just-in-time):** Do NOT offer it upfront. Wait until a question would genuinely be clearer shown than told — a real mockup / layout / diagram question, not merely a UI *topic*. The first time that happens, offer it then, as its own message:
> "This next part might be easier if I show you — I can put together mockups, diagrams, and comparisons in a browser tab as we go. It's still new and can be token-intensive. Want me to? I'll open it for you."

**This offer MUST be its own message.** Only the offer — no clarifying question, summary, or other content. Wait for the user's response. If they accept, start the server with `--open` so their browser opens to the first screen automatically. If they decline, continue text-only and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**

- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs
- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions

A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. "What does personality mean in this context?" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. "Which wizard layout works better?" is a visual question — use the browser.

If they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:
`skills/brainstorming/visual-companion.md`

# Spec: missions-draft

## Goal
Add DRAFT missions: create, edit, slots, list and show, in the API and the CLI (build step 4, `design/DESIGN.md:67`). Add the skill list, so that a lead can find skill IDs for slots. Move the API routes into a `routers` package and the CLI commands into a `commands` package, so that each later build step adds one module.

## Acceptance criteria
| ID | Criterion | The tests must prove |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 | The API follows the FastAPI "Bigger Applications" structure. The CLI has one module for each command group. Behaviour does not change. | `mc_api/main.py` contains no route function. Each router is in `mc_api/routers/`. `get_current_user` and `get_scope` are in `mc_api/dependencies.py`. The CLI commands are in `mc_cli/commands/`. All Step 3 tests pass without a change of their assertions. |
| AC2 | A director or a lead creates a mission (DESIGN 327). | `POST /missions` gives 201. The status is `DRAFT`. `lead_id` is the caller. The response has no slots. |
| AC3 | The API flags a mission that a director leads (DESIGN 199, 339-341). | `requires_additional_director` is true when the current role of the lead is `DIRECTOR`. It is false for a lead. A role change of the lead in the DB changes the flag of the existing mission. |
| AC4 | The API rejects wrong dates. | `end_date < start_date` gives 422 on create. On edit, the API checks the dates after it merges them with the stored values. A wrong merge gives 422. |
| AC5 | Directors and leads list all missions of the own org (DESIGN 331). | `GET /missions` returns each mission of the own org and no mission of another org. The order is newest `start_date` first. |
| AC6 | Directors and leads show a mission of the own org. | `GET /missions/{id}` returns the mission, the lead username, the flag and the active slots in position order. Archived slots are not in the response. |
| AC7 | The lead of the mission edits title, description and dates in DRAFT (DESIGN 273). | `PATCH /missions/{id}` with some fields changes only those fields. It gives 200 and the new mission. |
| AC8 | Only the lead of the mission edits it (DESIGN 323). | Another lead or a director of the own org gets 403 on PATCH and on both slot routes. The body is `{"role": "<ROLE>", "rule": "Directors and leads edit only their own missions"}`. |
| AC9 | Edits are allowed only in DRAFT (DESIGN 273). | For a mission in each other status, PATCH and both slot routes give 409. The body is `{"detail": "Mission is <STATUS>. Edits are allowed only in DRAFT."}`. |
| AC10 | The lead adds a slot in DRAFT (DESIGN 280-281). | `POST /missions/{id}/slots {skill_id, min_level}` gives 201 and the mission. The new slot has the lowest free position among the active slots. `min_level` outside 1 to 5 gives 422. |
| AC11 | The lead removes a slot in DRAFT. The API archives it (DESIGN 214, 283). | `DELETE /missions/{id}/slots/{position}` gives 200 and the mission without the slot. The row still exists with `archived_at` set. A position with no active slot gives 404. After the lead removes slot 2 of 3, the next new slot gets position 2. |
| AC12 | A slot names only a skill of the own org (DESIGN 355). | A `skill_id` that does not exist, or that belongs to another org, gives 422 with the body `{"detail": "Unknown skill: <id>"}`. Both cases give the same body. |
| AC13 | Crew members have no access to missions in this step (DESIGN 331). | A crew member gets 403 on each mission route, for each ID. The body is `{"role": "CREW", "rule": "Only directors and leads manage and view missions"}`. |
| AC14 | A mission of another org is not visible (DESIGN req 4, 22). | A director and a lead of org A each get 404 for a mission of org B on GET, PATCH, POST slots and DELETE slots. Each body equals the body for a random UUID: `{"detail": "Not found"}`. The mission of org B does not change. |
| AC15 | Each user lists the skills of the own org. | `GET /skills` gives 200 for each role. It returns `id`, `name` and `description` of each skill of the own org, sorted by name. It returns no skill of another org. |
| AC16 | The CLI runs the mission commands (DESIGN 423-425). | `mc missions create`, `edit`, `list`, `show`, `mc missions slots add` and `remove`, and `mc skills list` each call the API and show the result. `create` of a director-led mission prints "This mission needs an additional director for approval." |
| AC17 | The CLI shows a clear error for 409 and 422. | For 409, the output contains the `detail`. For 422 with a text `detail`, the output contains the text. For 422 with a FastAPI validation list, the output contains `<field>: <message>` for each item. Each exits 1 with no traceback. |

## Non-goals
- Slot update. The lead removes a slot and adds a new one.
- Filters for `mc missions list`.
- Crew access to mission details. Steps 7 and 9 add it through assignments.
- A way to clear the description.
- A schema change or a migration. The `mission` and `mission_requirement` tables of step 2 have all the columns.
- Submit, approve and the other transitions (step 6 and step 8). The matcher (step 5).
- Short references for missions and skills (P1, DESIGN 82).
- An `internal/` package. Step 4 has no admin routes.

## End-to-end check
| # | Action | Expected result | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `mc login --user leo`, then `mc skills list` | Exit 0. The output has the 6 skills of "Artemis Space Agency" with their IDs. It does not have `Welding`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_missions_cli.py` |
| 2 | `mc missions create --title "Ice Core Drill" --start 2027-03-01 --end 2027-03-10` | Exit 0. The output has the mission ID and `DRAFT`. It has no additional director message. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_missions_cli.py` |
| 3 | `mc missions slots add <id> --skill <Piloting id> --level 3`, then the same with `<Geology id> --level 2` | Exit 0 each. The output shows slot 1 Piloting and slot 2 Geology. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_missions_cli.py` |
| 4 | `mc missions slots remove <id> 1`, then `mc missions slots add <id> --skill <EVA id> --level 3` | Exit 0 each. The output shows slot 1 EVA and slot 2 Geology. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_missions_cli.py` |
| 5 | `mc missions edit <id> --title "Ice Core Drill II"` | Exit 0. The output has the new title. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_missions_cli.py` |
| 6 | `mc missions list`, then `mc missions show <id>` | Exit 0 each. The list has the new mission and the 3 seeded missions of org A. `show` has the new title, `leo` and both slots. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_missions_cli.py` |
| 7 | `mc login --user nick`, then `mc missions show <id>` | Exit 1. The output contains `Not found`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_missions_cli.py` |
| 8 | `mc login --user ava`, then `mc missions list` | Exit 1. The output contains `CREW` and `Only directors and leads manage and view missions`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_missions_cli.py` |
| 9 | `mc login --user diana`, then `mc missions create --title "Deep Field Survey" --start 2027-04-01 --end 2027-04-05` | Exit 0. The output contains `This mission needs an additional director for approval.` | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_missions_cli.py` |

The E2E test uses the seed data and uvicorn on a free port, as the Step 3 E2E test does (`packages/api/tests/e2e/test_auth_cli.py:21-47`).

## Resolved questions
| Question | Answer | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Task name? | `missions-draft`, folder `.work/missions-draft/` | me |
| Which state does Step 4 start from? | Step 3 is complete as `.work/auth-tenant/plan.md` describes it. This includes `OrgScope.get` and `select`, `Forbidden` with its 403 handler, and `GET /users/{id}`. | me, `.work/auth-tenant/plan.md:211-226` |
| How does the lead change slots? | Add and remove only. To change a slot, the lead removes it and adds a new one. The archived row keeps the assignment history. | me |
| Which position does a new slot get? | The lowest free position among the active slots | me |
| How does the CLI name a skill? | By UUID, as DESIGN says for P0. `GET /skills` and `mc skills list` show the IDs. | me, `design/DESIGN.md:437` |
| Who can list skills? | Each role, own org only | me |
| What does an edit outside DRAFT return? | 409 with a `detail` that names the status. 403 stays for role rules. | me |
| What does an unknown or cross-org `skill_id` return? | 422 with `{"detail": "Unknown skill: <id>"}`, the same for both cases | me |
| What can crew do with missions? | Nothing in Step 4. They get 403 on each mission route. | me, `design/DESIGN.md:331` |
| Where does the crew check run? | In a router dependency on the missions router. A crew member gets 403 for each ID, also for an ID of another org. The response does not depend on the ID, so it does not leak the mission. This is an exception to "Return 404 for a resource in another org" for crew. | me |
| Which filters does `mc missions list` have? | None | me |
| How do two concurrent writes on one mission behave? | Each write loads the mission with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, then checks and commits. Writes on one mission run one after the other. | me, `design/DESIGN.md:303` |
| Who is the lead of a new mission? | The caller. Reassign is P2. | `design/DESIGN.md:96` |
| What is the check order of a mission write? | Crew 403 (router), then 404 for a missing or cross-org mission, then 403 for a non-owner, then 409 for a status other than DRAFT, then 422 for bad input | me, `design/DESIGN.md:377-381` |
| How is the API structured? | As the FastAPI tutorial "Bigger Applications": `main.py`, `dependencies.py`, and `routers/` with one `APIRouter` for each resource. Absolute imports, as in the codebase. | me, https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/#an-example-file-structure |
| Do the Step 3 routes move too? | Yes. `/health`, `/auth/login`, `/me` and `/users/{id}` move into `routers/`. `mc_api.main:app` keeps its name. | me, `packages/api/tests/conftest.py:61`, `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_auth_cli.py:31` |
| Does the CLI get the same structure? | Yes. `mc_cli/commands/` has `auth.py`, `skills.py` and `missions.py`. `mc login`, `mc whoami` and `mc logout` stay top-level. `mc_cli.main:app` keeps its name. | me, `packages/cli/pyproject.toml:8` |
| Does Step 4 need a migration? | No. The tables have all the columns. | `packages/api/src/mc_api/models.py:126-169` |
| Who commits a write? | Each write route commits. `get_session` does not commit. | `packages/api/src/mc_api/db.py:27-29` |

1	# Missions in DRAFT Implementation Plan
2	
3	> Run with /implement-plan /Users/janeshorst/Dev/mutinex-interview/.work/missions-draft/plan.md in a fresh context.
4	
5	**Goal:** Move the API routes into `mc_api/routers/` and the CLI commands into `mc_cli/commands/`. Then add the skill list, and the DRAFT missions with create, list, show, edit and slots, in the API and the CLI.
6	
7	**Architecture:** The API follows the FastAPI "Bigger Applications" structure. `main.py` includes one `APIRouter` for each resource. `dependencies.py` holds the shared dependencies. The missions router has a router-level role check for crew. Each mission write loads the mission with a row lock and checks the owner and the DRAFT status. Then it changes the rows and commits. The CLI has one Typer module for each command group.
8	
9	**Tech Stack:** Python 3.12, FastAPI 0.143, Pydantic 2, SQLAlchemy 2.1, Typer 0.27, httpx, Rich 15, pytest, Postgres 17.
10	
11	**Spec:** /Users/janeshorst/Dev/mutinex-interview/.work/missions-draft/spec.md
12	**Verify:** verify:full = `.claude/hooks/verify.sh full`; verify:fast = `.claude/hooks/verify.sh fast`
13	**Contract:** Covers, Tests must prove, Files, Interfaces, Global Constraints and Checkpoint are binding. Report each change to them to the human. The implementer chooses the code.
14	
15	## Global Constraints
16	
17	- Step 4 starts after Step 3 is complete, as `.work/auth-tenant/plan.md` describes it. Before slice 1, check that these parts exist: `OrgScope.get` and `OrgScope.select`, `mc_api/errors.py` with `Forbidden`, `GET /users/{id}`, and `error_message` for 403 and 404. If one is missing, stop and tell the human.
18	- Do not change the schema. `alembic check` on `mc_test` must report no difference (`packages/api/tests/test_migration.py`).
19	- Put each request and response type in `mc_shared`. It depends only on Pydantic (`packages/shared/pyproject.toml:6`).
20	- Use absolute imports (`from mc_api.x import ...`), as in the codebase. Do not use the relative imports of the FastAPI tutorial.
21	- `mc_api.main:app` and `mc_cli.main:app` keep their names. The tests, uvicorn and the `mc` script use them (`packages/api/tests/conftest.py:61`, `packages/cli/pyproject.toml:8`).
22	- Routers read tenant data only through `OrgScope`. Only `routers/health.py` (`SELECT 1`) and the login route take a raw `Session`.
23	- A missing row and a row of another org give the same 404 body: `{"detail": "Not found"}`.
24	- Exact error bodies:
25	  - Crew on a mission route: 403 `{"role": "CREW", "rule": "Only directors and leads manage and view missions"}`.
26	  - Non-owner: 403 `{"role": "<ROLE>", "rule": "Directors and leads edit only their own missions"}`.
27	  - Not DRAFT: 409 `{"detail": "Mission is <STATUS>. Edits are allowed only in DRAFT."}`.
28	  - Unknown skill: 422 `{"detail": "Unknown skill: <skill_id>"}`.
29	- Check order of a mission write: crew 403 (router dependency), then 404, then non-owner 403, then 409, then 422 for the body.
30	- Each mission write loads the mission with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` through `OrgScope.get(..., for_update=True)`. Then it checks, changes the rows and commits. `get_session` does not commit (`packages/api/src/mc_api/db.py:27-29`).
31	- `requires_additional_director` is derived from the current role of the lead. Never store it.
32	- Integration tests create their own orgs and users with `make_user` (`packages/api/tests/conftest.py:68-85`). No test assumes empty tables.
33	- The E2E tests have the marker `e2e` and use the seed data. verify:fast excludes them. verify:full runs them.
34	- Only the test writer edits paths that match `TEST_PATTERNS` in `.claude/project.sh:6-8` (`^packages/[^/]+/tests/`). This includes each `conftest.py`.
35	- Do not edit `BRIEF.md`.
36	
37	## Review Focus
38	
39	1. `PATCH /missions/{id}` with `{}` or with `{"title": null}`. Expected: 200 and no change, never 500. The API ignores a null field. Slice 4 tests it.
40	2. `POST /missions` with `"title": ""`. Expected: 422. Slice 3 tests it.
41	3. A mission ID that is not a UUID: `GET /missions/not-a-uuid` and `mc missions show abc`. Expected: 422 from the API. The CLI prints the field and the message, exits 1 and shows no traceback. Slice 3 tests it.
42	4. A wrong date in the CLI: `mc missions create ... --start 2027-13-01`. Expected: exit 1. The output names `start_date` and shows no traceback. Slice 3 tests it.
43	5. A slot position that has no active slot or is not a number: `DELETE /missions/{id}/slots/0` and `/slots/abc`. Expected: 404 for `0`, 422 for `abc`, never 500. Slice 5 tests it.

# Missions in DRAFT Implementation Plan

> Run with /implement-plan /Users/janeshorst/Dev/mutinex-interview/.work/missions-draft/plan.md in a fresh context.

**Goal:** Move the API routes into `mc_api/routers/` and the CLI commands into `mc_cli/commands/`. Then add the skill list, and the DRAFT missions with create, list, show, edit and slots, in the API and the CLI.

**Architecture:** The API follows the FastAPI "Bigger Applications" structure. `main.py` includes one `APIRouter` for each resource. `dependencies.py` holds the shared dependencies. The missions router has a router-level role check for crew. Each mission write loads the mission with a row lock and checks the owner and the DRAFT status. Then it changes the rows and commits. The CLI has one Typer module for each command group.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.12, FastAPI 0.143, Pydantic 2, SQLAlchemy 2.1, Typer 0.27, httpx, Rich 15, pytest, Postgres 17.

**Spec:** /Users/janeshorst/Dev/mutinex-interview/.work/missions-draft/spec.md
**Verify:** verify:full = `.claude/hooks/verify.sh full`; verify:fast = `.claude/hooks/verify.sh fast`
**Contract:** Covers, Tests must prove, Files, Interfaces, Global Constraints and Checkpoint are binding. Report each change to them to the human. The implementer chooses the code.

## Global Constraints

- Step 4 starts after Step 3 is complete, as `.work/auth-tenant/plan.md` describes it. Before slice 1, check that these parts exist: `OrgScope.get` and `OrgScope.select`, `mc_api/errors.py` with `Forbidden`, `GET /users/{id}`, and `error_message` for 403 and 404. If one is missing, stop and tell the human.
- Do not change the schema. `alembic check` on `mc_test` must report no difference (`packages/api/tests/test_migration.py`).
- Put each request and response type in `mc_shared`. It depends only on Pydantic (`packages/shared/pyproject.toml:6`).
- Use absolute imports (`from mc_api.x import ...`), as in the codebase. Do not use the relative imports of the FastAPI tutorial.
- `mc_api.main:app` and `mc_cli.main:app` keep their names. The tests, uvicorn and the `mc` script use them (`packages/api/tests/conftest.py:61`, `packages/cli/pyproject.toml:8`).
- Routers read tenant data only through `OrgScope`. Only `routers/health.py` (`SELECT 1`) and the login route take a raw `Session`.
- A missing row and a row of another org give the same 404 body: `{"detail": "Not found"}`.
- Exact error bodies:
  - Crew on a mission route: 403 `{"role": "CREW", "rule": "Only directors and leads manage and view missions"}`.
  - Non-owner: 403 `{"role": "<ROLE>", "rule": "Directors and leads edit only their own missions"}`.
  - Not DRAFT: 409 `{"detail": "Mission is <STATUS>. Edits are allowed only in DRAFT."}`.
  - Unknown skill: 422 `{"detail": "Unknown skill: <skill_id>"}`.
- Check order of a mission write: crew 403 (router dependency), then 404, then non-owner 403, then 409, then 422 for the body.
- Each mission write loads the mission with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` through `OrgScope.get(..., for_update=True)`. Then it checks, changes the rows and commits. `get_session` does not commit (`packages/api/src/mc_api/db.py:27-29`).
- `requires_additional_director` is derived from the current role of the lead. Never store it.
- Integration tests create their own orgs and users with `make_user` (`packages/api/tests/conftest.py:68-85`). No test assumes empty tables.
- The E2E tests have the marker `e2e` and use the seed data. verify:fast excludes them. verify:full runs them.
- Only the test writer edits paths that match `TEST_PATTERNS` in `.claude/project.sh:6-8` (`^packages/[^/]+/tests/`). This includes each `conftest.py`.
- Do not edit `BRIEF.md`.

## Review Focus

1. `PATCH /missions/{id}` with `{}` or with `{"title": null}`. Expected: 200 and no change, never 500. The API ignores a null field. Slice 4 tests it.
2. `POST /missions` with `"title": ""`. Expected: 422. Slice 3 tests it.
3. A mission ID that is not a UUID: `GET /missions/not-a-uuid` and `mc missions show abc`. Expected: 422 from the API. The CLI prints the field and the message, exits 1 and shows no traceback. Slice 3 tests it.
4. A wrong date in the CLI: `mc missions create ... --start 2027-13-01`. Expected: exit 1. The output names `start_date` and shows no traceback. Slice 3 tests it.
5. A slot position that has no active slot or is not a number: `DELETE /missions/{id}/slots/0` and `/slots/abc`. Expected: 404 for `0`, 422 for `abc`, never 500. Slice 5 tests it.

I have the answers I need. Next are the approaches, then the design.

## Approaches for the conflict check

1. **Checks in the router module (recommended).** `routers/profile.py` holds the routes and one helper that finds the active assignments of the caller. Steps 4 to 8 also put their rules in their router (`.work/missions-draft/plan.md:324-327`). Only the profile routes use this query.
2. **A separate `mc_api/conflicts.py` module.** This gives a unit-testable function, but it adds a layer that only one router uses.
3. **DB triggers.** A trigger can reject a conflict. But the error message is hard to control, and DESIGN keeps rules in the service layer (`design/DESIGN.md:303`).

## Design

**API (`routers/profile.py`, prefix `/profile`)**
- The router dependency `require_roles(CREW, rule="Only crew members manage a profile")` gives 403 to directors and leads on each route.
- `GET /profile` → `ProfileOut {username, display_name, org_name}`.
- `GET /profile/skills` → `[CrewSkillOut {skill_id, skill_name, level}]`, sorted by skill name.
- `PUT /profile/skills/{skill_id} {level}` → 200 `CrewSkillOut`. It adds the skill or updates the level. `level` outside 1 to 5 gives 422. A skill that is missing or in another org gives 422 `{"detail": "Unknown skill: <id>"}`, as step 4 does.
- `DELETE /profile/skills/{skill_id}` → 204. A skill that is not in the profile gives 404.
- `GET /profile/unavailability` → `[UnavailabilityOut {id, start_date, end_date, reason}]`, sorted by `start_date`.
- `POST /profile/unavailability {start_date, end_date, reason}` → 201 `UnavailabilityOut`. `end_date < start_date` gives 422.
- `DELETE /profile/unavailability/{id}` → 204. An entry of another user or another org gives 404.
- Check order: 401, then crew 403, then 404 or 422, then 409 conflict.

**Conflict check (writes only)**
- Each write first locks the caller row: `scope.get(AppUser, user.id, for_update=True)`.
- The helper loads each INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller, with its mission and slot. There is no mission status filter, because you selected the literal DESIGN rule.
- Rules (DESIGN 308-312):
  - A new entry overlaps the mission dates. Both ranges include their end dates.
  - A new level is below `min_level` of a slot with that skill.
  - A removed skill is the skill of a slot.
- Response: 409. The text `detail` has one line for each conflict, sorted by mission start date. Example: `Conflicts with your INVITED assignment on mission 'Orbital Debris Survey' (<id>): slot 2 requires Robotics level 3.`
- For an entry, the line ends with `the mission runs 2026-12-07 to 2026-12-18.`
- Each write and each 409 logs one info line.

**Shared types (`mc_shared`)**
- New types: `ProfileOut`, `CrewSkillOut`, `SkillLevel {level: 1..5}`, `UnavailabilityCreate` (with the date validator) and `UnavailabilityOut`.
- `UnavailabilityReason` moves to `mc_shared`, as `MissionStatus` does in step 4. The DB enum name does not change.

**CLI (`commands/profile.py`)**
- `mc profile show` prints `ava (Ava Lindqvist), org Artemis Space Agency`.
- `mc profile skills list` prints a table with the columns `Skill ID`, `Skill` and `Level`.
- `mc profile skills set <skill-id> --level n` prints `Set Robotics to level 4`.
- `mc profile skills remove <skill-id>` prints `Removed skill <id>`.
- `mc profile availability list` prints a table with the columns `ID`, `From`, `To` and `Reason`.
- `mc profile availability add --from <date> --to <date> --reason HOLIDAY|SICK|MEETING`: all three options are required. It prints `Added unavailability <id>`.
- `mc profile availability remove <id>` prints `Removed unavailability <id>`.

**Tests**
- Integration tests use `make_user` orgs.
- E2E tests (`e2e/test_profile_cli.py`) use the seed data:
  - ava (no assignments): the full skill and availability journey.
  - hana: Robotics 4, INVITED on "Orbital Debris Survey", 2026-12-07 to 2026-12-18, slot 2 Robotics level 3. Robotics level 2 gives a 409. Leave on 2026-12-10 gives a 409.
  - nell of org B sets an org A skill: 422.
  - diana: 403 with the rule.

# Spec: crew-profile

## Goal
Add the crew profile of build step 9 (`design/DESIGN.md:72`) to the API and the CLI. A crew member shows their profile, and lists and changes their own skills and unavailability. The API rejects a change that conflicts with an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment (`design/DESIGN.md:305-312`).

## Acceptance criteria
| ID | Criterion | The tests must prove |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 | Only crew members use the profile routes (DESIGN 335). | A director and a lead each get 403 on each `/profile` route. The body is `{"role": "<ROLE>", "rule": "Only crew members manage a profile"}`. A request without a token gets 401. |
| AC2 | A crew member shows their profile. | `GET /profile` gives 200 and exactly `{"username", "display_name", "org_name"}` of the caller. |
| AC3 | A crew member lists their own skills (DESIGN 12). | `GET /profile/skills` gives 200 and one item `{"skill_id", "skill_name", "level"}` for each own skill, sorted by skill name. It has no skill of another user. |
| AC4 | A crew member adds a skill or changes its level (DESIGN 12, 431). | `PUT /profile/skills/{skill_id} {"level": n}` gives 200 and the crew skill. A skill that is not in the profile is added. A skill in the profile gets the new level. `level` outside 1 to 5 gives 422. |
| AC5 | A skill names only a skill of the own org (DESIGN 355). | `PUT` with a `skill_id` that does not exist, or that belongs to another org, gives 422 with `{"detail": "Unknown skill: <id>"}`. Both cases give the same body. No row changes. |
| AC6 | A crew member removes a skill (DESIGN 12, 431). | `DELETE /profile/skills/{skill_id}` gives 204. The skill is not in `GET /profile/skills`. A skill that is not in the profile gives 404 `{"detail": "Not found"}`. |
| AC7 | A crew member lists their own unavailability (DESIGN 13, 432). | `GET /profile/unavailability` gives 200 and each own entry, past and future, as `{"id", "start_date", "end_date", "reason"}`, sorted by `start_date`. It has no entry of another user. |
| AC8 | A crew member adds unavailability (DESIGN 13, 432). | `POST /profile/unavailability {"start_date", "end_date", "reason"}` gives 201 and the entry. A one-day entry is valid. An entry that overlaps an own entry is valid. `end_date < start_date` gives 422. A missing or unknown `reason` gives 422. |
| AC9 | A crew member removes their own unavailability (DESIGN 13, 178). | `DELETE /profile/unavailability/{id}` gives 204. An ID of another crew member of the own org, of another org, or a random UUID gives 404 `{"detail": "Not found"}`. The other entry does not change. |
| AC10 | The API rejects an entry that overlaps an active assignment (DESIGN 310). | An entry that overlaps the dates of a mission with an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller gives 409. An overlap of one day at either end counts. No row is added. A DECLINED or CANCELLED assignment does not block. |
| AC11 | The API rejects a level below the minimum of an active slot (DESIGN 311). | `PUT` with a level below `min_level` of a slot of an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller with that skill gives 409. A level equal to `min_level` gives 200. The stored level does not change after a 409. |
| AC12 | The API rejects removal of a skill that an active slot requires (DESIGN 312). | `DELETE` of a skill that is the skill of a slot of an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller gives 409. The skill stays in the profile. |
| AC13 | Each INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment blocks, for each mission status. | An ACCEPTED assignment on a COMPLETED mission blocks a lower level. |
| AC14 | The 409 body names each conflict (DESIGN 306). | The body is `{"detail": "<lines>"}` with one line for each conflict, sorted by mission start date. A skill line is `Conflicts with your <STATUS> assignment on mission '<title>' (<mission_id>): slot <position> requires <skill> level <min_level>.` An entry line is `Conflicts with your <STATUS> assignment on mission '<title>' (<mission_id>): the mission runs <start_date> to <end_date>.` |
| AC15 | Profile data of another org is not visible (DESIGN req 4, 22). | A crew member of org B gets 422 on `PUT` and 404 on `DELETE` with a skill of org A. A crew member of org B gets 404 on `DELETE` of an entry of org A. The org A rows do not change. |
| AC16 | The CLI runs the profile commands (DESIGN 430-432). | `mc profile show`, `mc profile skills list\|set\|remove` and `mc profile availability list\|add\|remove` each call the API and show the result. `add` requires `--from`, `--to` and `--reason`. A 403, 404, 409 or 422 exits 1 with the API message and no traceback. |

## Non-goals
- Skills and unavailability in `mc profile show`. The list commands show them.
- The org crew view for directors and leads. It is build step 10 (`design/DESIGN.md:73`).
- A change of an existing unavailability entry. The crew member removes it and adds a new one.
- A check of own overlapping entries or of past dates.
- A mission status filter in the conflict check. An ACCEPTED assignment on a COMPLETED mission blocks a lower level forever, unless a later step changes its status.
- A schema change or a migration. The `crew_skill` and `unavailability` tables of step 2 have all the columns.
- Short references for skills (P1, `design/DESIGN.md:82`).

## End-to-end check
| # | Action | Expected result | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `mc login --user ava`, then `mc profile show` | Exit 0. The output contains `ava`, `Ava Lindqvist` and `Artemis Space Agency`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 2 | `mc profile skills list` | Exit 0. The output has `Piloting` with level 5 and `Communications` with level 4. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 3 | `mc profile skills set <EVA id> --level 2`, then `mc profile skills set <Piloting id> --level 4`, then `mc profile skills list` | Exit 0 each. The list has `EVA` 2 and `Piloting` 4. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 4 | `mc profile skills remove <EVA id>`, then `mc profile skills list` | Exit 0 each. The list does not have `EVA`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 5 | `mc profile availability add --from 2027-03-01 --to 2027-03-05 --reason HOLIDAY`, then `mc profile availability list` | Exit 0 each. The add output has `Added unavailability <id>`. The list has the entry with `2027-03-01`, `2027-03-05` and `HOLIDAY`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 6 | `mc profile availability remove <id>`, then `mc profile availability list` | Exit 0 each. The list does not have the entry. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 7 | `mc login --user hana`, then `mc profile skills set <Robotics id> --level 2` | Exit 1. The output contains `Orbital Debris Survey`, `INVITED` and `Robotics level 3`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 8 | As hana, `mc profile availability add --from 2026-12-10 --to 2026-12-10 --reason SICK` | Exit 1. The output contains `Orbital Debris Survey` and `2026-12-07 to 2026-12-18`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 9 | `mc login --user nell` (org B), then `mc profile skills set <org A Medicine id> --level 3` | Exit 1. The output contains `Unknown skill`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 10 | `mc login --user diana`, then `mc profile show` | Exit 1. The output contains `DIRECTOR` and `Only crew members manage a profile`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |

The E2E test uses the seed data and the `api_url` and `mc` fixtures of `packages/api/tests/e2e/conftest.py` (`.work/missions-draft/plan.md:121`). The skill IDs come from `mc skills list` (`.work/missions-draft/plan.md:179`).

| Which state does step 9 start from? | Step 4 is complete as `.work/missions-draft/plan.md` describes it. This includes `routers/`, `commands/`, `dependencies.require_roles`, `OrgScope.get(..., for_update=True)`, `GET /skills`, `mc skills list`, the 409 and 422 CLI messages and `e2e/conftest.py`. Steps 5 to 8 are not necessary. | me, `.work/missions-draft/plan.md:121,169-176,242,282,321` |

| What does `GET /profile` return? | A new type `ProfileOut` with `username`, `display_name` and `org_name` only. Skills and unavailability have their own list routes, so the profile route does not load them. | me |
| Which roles use `/profile`? | Crew only. A router dependency gives 403 with the rule `Only crew members manage a profile` on each route. | me, `design/DESIGN.md:335` |
| Which assignments block a profile change? | Each INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller, for each mission status | me, `design/DESIGN.md:306` |
| What is the 409 body? | A text `detail` with one line for each conflict. The step 4 CLI prints a 409 text `detail`. | me, `.work/missions-draft/plan.md:282` |

| Which entries does the API accept? | Each range with `end_date >= start_date`. Own overlap and past dates are allowed. The conflict check still applies. | me |
| Which entries does the availability list show? | All own entries, sorted by `start_date` | me |

| What do the write routes return? | Only the changed item. `PUT` skill gives 200 and the crew skill. `POST` entry gives 201 and the entry. Each `DELETE` gives 204. The CLI prints one line for each write. | me |
| What does `PUT` return for an unknown or cross-org skill? | 422 `{"detail": "Unknown skill: <id>"}`, as step 4 does for slots | me, `.work/missions-draft/spec.md` AC12 |

# Spec: crew-profile

## Goal
Add the crew profile of build step 9 (`design/DESIGN.md:72`) to the API and the CLI. A crew member shows their profile, and lists and changes their own skills and unavailability. The API rejects a change that conflicts with an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment (`design/DESIGN.md:305-312`).

## Acceptance criteria
| ID | Criterion | The tests must prove |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 | Only crew members use the profile routes (DESIGN 335). | A director and a lead each get 403 on each `/profile` route. The body is `{"role": "<ROLE>", "rule": "Only crew members manage a profile"}`. A request without a token gets 401. |
| AC2 | A crew member shows their profile. | `GET /profile` gives 200 and exactly `{"username", "display_name", "org_name"}` of the caller. |
| AC3 | A crew member lists their own skills (DESIGN 12). | `GET /profile/skills` gives 200 and one item `{"skill_id", "skill_name", "level"}` for each own skill, sorted by skill name. It has no skill of another user. |
| AC4 | A crew member adds a skill or changes its level (DESIGN 12, 431). | `PUT /profile/skills/{skill_id} {"level": n}` gives 200 and the crew skill. A skill that is not in the profile is added. A skill in the profile gets the new level. `level` outside 1 to 5 gives 422. |
| AC5 | A skill names only a skill of the own org (DESIGN 355). | `PUT` with a `skill_id` that does not exist, or that belongs to another org, gives 422 with `{"detail": "Unknown skill: <id>"}`. Both cases give the same body. No row changes. |
| AC6 | A crew member removes a skill (DESIGN 12, 431). | `DELETE /profile/skills/{skill_id}` gives 204. The skill is not in `GET /profile/skills`. A skill that is not in the profile gives 404 `{"detail": "Not found"}`. |
| AC7 | A crew member lists their own unavailability (DESIGN 13, 432). | `GET /profile/unavailability` gives 200 and each own entry, past and future, as `{"id", "start_date", "end_date", "reason"}`, sorted by `start_date`. It has no entry of another user. |
| AC8 | A crew member adds unavailability (DESIGN 13, 432). | `POST /profile/unavailability {"start_date", "end_date", "reason"}` gives 201 and the entry. A one-day entry is valid. An entry that overlaps an own entry is valid. `end_date < start_date` gives 422. A missing or unknown `reason` gives 422. |
| AC9 | A crew member removes their own unavailability (DESIGN 13, 178). | `DELETE /profile/unavailability/{id}` gives 204. An ID of another crew member of the own org, of another org, or a random UUID gives 404 `{"detail": "Not found"}`. The other entry does not change. |
| AC10 | The API rejects an entry that overlaps an active assignment (DESIGN 310). | An entry that overlaps the dates of a mission with an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller gives 409. An overlap of one day at either end counts. No row is added. A DECLINED or CANCELLED assignment does not block. |
| AC11 | The API rejects a level below the minimum of an active slot (DESIGN 311). | `PUT` with a level below `min_level` of a slot of an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller with that skill gives 409. A level equal to `min_level` gives 200. The stored level does not change after a 409. |
| AC12 | The API rejects removal of a skill that an active slot requires (DESIGN 312). | `DELETE` of a skill that is the skill of a slot of an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller gives 409. The skill stays in the profile. |
